speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I am here to help identify the cause of your acute diarrhea. To start, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if you have had any recent travel or exposure to sick contacts?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent levofloxacin use and the onset of watery diarrhea, I am concerned about Clostridioides difficile infection. Do you have any fever or blood in your stool, and have you had any significant abdominal distension?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, thank you for confirming those symptoms. To help rule out other causes and assess severity, do you have any fever or nausea, and have you noticed any blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Currently being treated for community-acquired pneumonia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travel or dietary changes reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To further assess the severity of your condition and check for signs of systemic involvement, have you experienced any dizziness, lightheadedness, or a significant decrease in urine output?

speaker: Patient
text: No fever, no recent antibiotics usage apart from levofloxacin for pneumonia, no vomiting, no blood in stool.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of recent levofloxacin use followed by acute watery diarrhea strongly suggests C. difficile infection, so I will order a stool test to confirm. REQUEST TEST: Stool_C_diff_toxin_assay

speaker: Doctor
text: The stool test result is inconclusive, so I need to assess for signs of severe infection or complications. Do you have an elevated white blood cell count or evidence of acute kidney injury, and has your abdominal pain worsened significantly?

speaker: Patient
text: No fever, no recent antibiotics usage apart from levofloxacin for pneumonia, no vomiting, no blood in stool.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to confirm the diagnosis and assess for complications, so I will request blood work to check for leukocytosis and renal function. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Basic_Metabolic_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: Hemoglobin: 13 g/dL, Total_Count_WBC: 13,400/mm3, Differential_Count: Neutrophils: 80%, Lymphocytes: 15%, Monocytes: 5%. Basic_Metabolic_Panel: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The leukocytosis supports the suspicion of C. difficile infection, so I will request a more specific diagnostic test to confirm the presence of the toxin. REQUEST TEST: Stool_C_diff_toxin_EIA

speaker: Doctor
text: The diagnostic tests for C. difficile toxin remain unspecified, but the clinical presentation of acute watery diarrhea following levofloxacin therapy, combined with leukocytosis, is highly indicative of C. difficile infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection
